title: core.phys.body — mass, centre of mass, inertia, densities
description: Rigid-body mass properties in SI units. The inertia tensor is symmetric, so it is stored as its six independent components in a DECLARED order rather than as a 3x3 array whose transposition nobody can check.

space.description: MODEL SPACE (S10-3, RULING, implemented). Every position and every axis in this node - center_of_mass_m and the inertia frame alike - is expressed in the entity model space, the same space core.phys.bounds uses. It is declared here because it previously was not: this schema required center_of_mass_m while saying nothing about the space it was in, its sibling core.phys.bounds declares const 'model', its sibling core.phys.colliders declares const 'part-local' and states in its own description that 'model space or part space is exactly the question a reader must not have to guess' - so the one field a reader had to guess about was in the family that forbids guessing. The only previous evidence was an inference from a sibling key (inertia.frame, const 'model-axes'), and the ruling agrees with it, so no existing conformant package changes meaning. The consequence worth stating: a transform sits between colliders and this node, and it is the part transform in MANIFEST.json parts[]. See spec/SPEC.md section 3.6a.

center_of_mass_m.description: Model space (declared by `space` above, S10-3), metres. Not part-local: core.phys.colliders is the part-local one of this family.

about.description: The point the tensor is taken about. Stating it removes the single most common inertia bug: a tensor about the origin used as if it were about the centre of mass.

frame.description: The tensor is expressed in the entity's model axes, NOT in its principal axes. principal_axes below gives the diagonalisation for consumers that want it.

component_order.description: Declared explicitly. The full tensor is [[ixx,-ixy,-ixz],[-ixy,iyy,-iyz],[-ixz,-iyz,izz]] using the PRODUCTS-OF-INERTIA sign convention, i.e. ixy = integral of x*y dm and it enters the matrix negated. Half the physics literature stores the negated value directly; werk stores the positive integral and negates on assembly, and says so here.

components_kg_m2.description: In the order given by component_order. Units kg*m^2.

principal_axes.description: Optional diagonalisation: the rotation taking model axes into principal axes, and the three principal moments in that frame.

densities.description: Per-material density used to arrive at the mass. Present so a consumer can recompute mass after scaling or after swapping a material, rather than accepting a number it cannot check.

hollow.description: True when the region was treated as a shell rather than a solid.

shell_thickness_m.description: Required in spirit when hollow is true.

method.description: How mass properties were computed, e.g. 'divergence-theorem-over-triangles', 'voxel-1mm', 'authored'.

static.description: Dimensionless Coulomb coefficient against a reference dry steel plate.

restitution.description: Coefficient of restitution against the same reference plate.

reference_surface.description: Friction is a property of a PAIR of surfaces, never of one. The reference surface is named so the numbers mean something.
